claims.text: Adding 2–4 at% Ti to a conventional high-entropy alloy will induce coherent nano-precipitate formation.
The resulting coherent nano-precipitates will simultaneously improve strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance.
The baseline alloy has a uniform multi-principal-element composition and does not naturally form controlled nano-precipitates.
Optimized heat treatment after Ti addition will promote nucleation and growth of coherent nano-precipitates.
The expected improvement requires uniformly distributed, nano-sized, coherent precipitates.
Inappropriate heat-treatment temperatures or cooling rates can produce coarse or incoherent precipitates.
Coarse or incoherent precipitates can cause embrittlement or insufficient strengthening.
Coherent nano-precipitates maintain a continuous ductile matrix.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength through particle strengthening.
The precipitates increase fracture resistance by blunting crack propagation.
Stiff precipitates increase Young’s modulus through improved load sharing.
The modified alloy should have approximately 10–20% greater yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy should have greater ductility and fracture toughness than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy should have a modestly greater Young’s modulus than the baseline alloy.
Exceeding the optimal Ti concentration may produce coarse or incoherent precipitates and degrade ductility or fracture resistance.
The magnitude of improvement depends on Ti concentration, processing conditions, and the particular base-alloy system.
